anchor.name: nano-Cu heat-capacity bulk-reuse prior
anchor.scientific_claim_under_test: For same-composition fcc Cu with approximately 8 nm grains and no phase transition, ordinary bulk Cu Cp(T) should remain a good zeroth-order quantitative baseline, with at most a small percent-scale excess.
anchor.counterevidence_route: A literature-grounded approximately 10% nanocrystalline Cu Cp enhancement over the 150–300 K interval.

adjudications.label: GPT-4.1
adjudications.reason: Bulk Cu is the expected baseline; only a small nanocrystalline heat-capacity excess was expected.

adjudications.label: GPT-5.6
adjudications.reason: Bulk-like Cp is the zeroth-order expectation; order-percent deviations are plausible while a roughly ten-percent excess is surprising.

adjudications.label: DeepSeek-v4-pro
adjudications.reason: Expected nanocrystalline Cu to remain close to bulk, with only approximately percent-scale excess.

adjudications.label: Claude-opus-5
adjudications.reason: Expected a small positive excess, approximately a few percent, rather than a large Cp enhancement.

adjudications.label: GLM-5.2
adjudications.reason: Explicitly expected roughly 1–5% excess and stated that a difference exceeding about 10% would be surprising.

adjudications.label: Kimi-k3
adjudications.reason: Kimi explicitly retained bulk Cu as the quantitative baseline and expected only an approximately 1-3% Cp excess, with roughly 0-5% as a reasonable range. The frozen approximately 10% enhancement therefore lies outside its ordinary prior expectation.

important_note: All six canonical models completed the 8-nm Gate-0. All six are PRIOR_HELD. Kimi's earlier provider failure was resolved by its later canonical retry.
